problem_checks.assumptions_verified: alpha=0; S={00} union {1^n:n>=1} is a computable convex prefix forest. U0=S and U1={00} are computable upward-closed subsets of S, with height>index; their path sets are {1^omega} and empty, hence disjoint on a nonempty domain.
problem_checks.decisive_check: At 00 there is no proper predecessor in S, so both printed membership tests succeed. Equality makes 00 comparable to itself, violating orthogonality. This is an exact analytic witness; finite truncation is not used to establish infinite-domain assumptions.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_limits: The existence lemma is not refuted: W0=S,W1=empty works for this input. The repair uses a computable forest, as explicitly qualified in the report and in the inspected effective applications. No new blanket assumption is attributed to the displayed lemma.
problem_checks.repair_verification: Taking the first ancestor in the union, resolving same-node ties by least index, and inheriting its owner is uniformly computable because index<height makes the search finite. Upward closure preserves membership; a true path cannot change to a competing owner without entering both disjoint path sets.
problem_checks.core_dependency: The missing unique-owner guarantee is explicitly used in Proposition3.17 gluing p15, Proposition4.9 limit p28, separator-name definition p34 and Proposition2.14 p49. Major assesses this invalid core construction, not a false determinacy theorem.
